definition: To cut wood, stone, or meat into a shape or into pieces.
examples: Dad carved the turkey.
He carved a bird from a piece of wood.
We're carving pumpkins for Halloween.

spanish.definition: Cortar madera, piedra o carne en una forma o en pedazos.

definition: To hide something.
examples: She tried to conceal her anger.
He concealed the gun under his coat.
They're concealing the truth from us.

spanish.definition: Esconder algo.

definition: To move text up or down on a screen.
examples: Scroll down to the bottom of the page.
I scrolled through my photos.
She's always scrolling on her phone.

spanish.definition: Mover un texto hacia arriba o hacia abajo en una pantalla.

definition: To make something tighter.
examples: Tighten your seat belt.
He tightened the screws.
She's tightening the rope.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más apretado.

definition: To use, eat, or drink something.
examples: This car consumes a lot of gas.
Americans consume a lot of sugar.
He's consumed by guilt.

spanish.definition: Usar, comer o tomar algo.

definition: To give things to many people.
examples: They distributed food to the families.
The teacher distributed the tests.
We're distributing flyers downtown.

spanish.definition: Dar cosas a muchas personas.

definition: To put something into something else.
examples: Insert your card here.
She inserted the key into the lock.
He's inserting a photo into the document.

spanish.definition: Poner algo dentro de otra cosa.

definition: To look at something carefully.
examples: The mechanic inspected the brakes.
Someone will inspect the house tomorrow.
They're inspecting all of the bags.

spanish.definition: Mirar algo con cuidado.

definition: To make beer or coffee.
examples: He brews his own beer.
I brewed a fresh pot of coffee.
They're brewing a new beer in Denver.

spanish.definition: Hacer cerveza o café.

definition: To make someone want to do something.
examples: The cake tempted me.
Don't tempt me!
I was tempted to quit.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien quiera hacer algo.

definition: To end something; to decide something after thinking.
examples: The police concluded it was an accident.
She concluded her speech with a joke.
We're concluding the meeting now.

spanish.definition: Terminar algo; decidir algo después de pensar.

definition: To fight by holding and pushing someone to the ground.
examples: The boys wrestled on the grass.
He wrestled in high school.
She's wrestling with a hard decision.

spanish.definition: Pelear agarrando y empujando a alguien hacia el suelo.

definition: To take in a liquid or information.
examples: The towel absorbed the water.
Plants absorb water through their roots.
It's hard to absorb so much information.

spanish.definition: Tomar un líquido o información.

definition: To put medicine into the body with a needle.
examples: The nurse injected the medicine.
He has to inject himself with insulin.
They're injecting the dog with a vaccine.

spanish.definition: Meter medicina en el cuerpo con una aguja.

definition: To go down.
examples: The plane began to descend.
We descended the stairs slowly.
They're descending the mountain now.

spanish.definition: Bajar.

definition: To feel very sad because someone has died.
examples: She's still grieving for her husband.
The town grieved after the accident.
Everyone grieves in a different way.

spanish.definition: Sentir mucha tristeza porque alguien murió.

definition: To join together.
examples: The two banks merged last year.
Cars merge onto the highway here.
They're merging the two classes.

spanish.definition: Unirse.

definition: To not give enough care to something.
examples: He neglected his children.
Don't neglect your health.
The old house suffered years of neglect.

spanish.definition: No darle suficiente cuidado a algo.

definition: To choose someone for a job.
examples: They appointed her as manager.
The president appointed a new judge.
Who's appointing the new director?

spanish.definition: Elegir a alguien para un trabajo.

definition: To break a rule or a law.
examples: He violated the terms of his contract.
You can't violate the law.
They're violating our agreement.

spanish.definition: Romper una regla o una ley.

definition: To move in small, quick movements.
examples: The baby wiggled her toes.
Can you wiggle your ears?
The dog is wiggling with joy.

spanish.definition: Moverse con movimientos pequeños y rápidos.

definition: To breathe in.
examples: Inhale slowly through your nose.
He inhaled the smoke.
She's inhaling the smell of the flowers.

spanish.definition: Tomar aire.

definition: To look like someone or something.
examples: She resembles her mother.
This story resembles another book I read.
The two houses closely resemble each other.

spanish.definition: Verse como alguien o algo.

definition: To mix playing cards; to walk slowly without lifting your feet.
examples: Please shuffle the cards.
The old man shuffled across the room.
He's shuffling through his papers.

spanish.definition: Mezclar cartas; caminar despacio sin levantar los pies.

definition: To stop something for a time; to keep a student out of school as punishment.
examples: The school suspended him for three days.
They suspended the game because of rain.
The bank is suspending my account.

spanish.definition: Detener algo por un tiempo; sacar a un estudiante de la escuela como castigo.

definition: To judge the value or quality of something.
examples: We need to assess the damage.
The test assesses your reading level.
Doctors are assessing his condition.

spanish.definition: Juzgar el valor o la calidad de algo.

definition: To be not the same.
examples: Prices differ from store to store.
Our opinions differ on this.
The two languages differed a lot.

spanish.definition: No ser igual.

definition: To crush food until it is soft.
examples: Mash the potatoes with some butter.
She mashed a banana for the baby.
He's mashing the beans with a fork.

spanish.definition: Aplastar comida hasta que quede suave.

definition: To expect something to happen.
examples: We don't anticipate any problems.
I didn't anticipate so much traffic.
They're anticipating a big crowd.

spanish.definition: Esperar que algo pase.

definition: To close or attach something.
examples: Please fasten your seat belt.
She fastened the buttons on her coat.
He's fastening the sign to the wall.

spanish.definition: Cerrar o sujetar algo.

definition: To build something.
examples: They constructed a bridge over the river.
The house was constructed in 1920.
We're constructing a new school.

spanish.definition: Edificar algo.

definition: To do something without planning it first.
examples: I forgot my notes, so I had to improvise.
Jazz musicians love to improvise.
We're improvising because we don't have the right tools.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo sin planearlo antes.

definition: To show that something is important; the best part of something.
examples: Highlight the main points in yellow.
The report highlighted the problem.
The trip was the highlight of my year.

spanish.definition: Mostrar que algo es importante; la mejor parte de algo.

definition: To fail to notice something; to have a view of something.
examples: I overlooked a small mistake.
Our room overlooks the ocean.
They're overlooking an important fact.

spanish.definition: No notar algo; tener vista hacia algo.

definition: To break a connection.
examples: The phone company disconnected our line.
Disconnect the printer from the computer.
We got disconnected during the call.

spanish.definition: Romper una conexión.

definition: To see the difference between things.
examples: He can't distinguish red from green.
It's hard to distinguish the twins.
What distinguishes this phone from the others?

spanish.definition: Ver la diferencia entre las cosas.

definition: To find the way to a place.
examples: Sailors used the stars to navigate.
She navigated through the crowded streets.
I'm navigating; you just drive.

spanish.definition: Encontrar el camino a un lugar.

definition: To mix with a liquid and disappear into it.
examples: Sugar dissolves in hot water.
Dissolve the salt in a cup of water.
The tablet is dissolving in the glass.

spanish.definition: Mezclarse con un líquido y desaparecer en él.

definition: To complain in a sad, annoying voice.
examples: Stop whining about the food.
The dog whined at the door.
The kids are whining because they're tired.

spanish.definition: Quejarse con una voz triste y molesta.

definition: To break into small pieces.
examples: The old wall crumbled.
She crumbled the cheese over the salad.
The cookie is crumbling in my hand.

spanish.definition: Romperse en pedazos pequeños.

definition: A garden tool with a long handle; to collect leaves with this tool.
examples: I raked the leaves in the yard.
Put the rake back in the garage.
She's raking the grass.

spanish.definition: Herramienta de jardín con mango largo; recoger hojas con esta herramienta.

definition: To tell people about a product so they buy it.
examples: They advertise on TV.
The company advertised the job online.
We're advertising our new menu.

spanish.definition: Contarle a la gente sobre un producto para que lo compre.

definition: To make something possible.
examples: The loan enabled her to buy a house.
This app enables you to pay by phone.
Please enable your camera.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo sea posible.

definition: To turn around a center point; to take turns.
examples: The Earth rotates once a day.
Rotate the picture to the left.
The nurses are rotating shifts.

spanish.definition: Girar alrededor de un punto central; turnarse.

definition: To move your eyebrows together because you are unhappy.
examples: She frowned when she saw the bill.
Why are you frowning?
He looked at me with a frown.

spanish.definition: Juntar las cejas porque no estás contento.

definition: To tell someone what to do; to teach.
examples: The doctor instructed me to rest.
She instructs new employees.
We were instructed to stay inside.

spanish.definition: Decirle a alguien qué hacer; enseñar.

definition: To copy someone or something.
examples: Babies imitate their parents.
He can imitate the president's voice.
Stop imitating me!

spanish.definition: Copiar a alguien o algo.

definition: To watch people and make sure they do things correctly.
examples: She supervises a team of ten.
An adult must supervise the children.
He's supervising the new workers.

spanish.definition: Vigilar a la gente y asegurarse de que haga las cosas bien.

definition: To say officially what medicine a patient should take.
examples: The doctor prescribed some pills.
She prescribes medicine for his heart.
Why are they prescribing so many drugs?

spanish.definition: Decir de forma oficial qué medicina debe tomar un paciente.

definition: To make a loud noise while sleeping.
examples: My husband snores very loudly.
The dog snored all night.
He was snoring on the sofa.

spanish.definition: Hacer un ruido fuerte mientras duermes.

definition: To move your finger across a screen; to pass a card through a machine.
examples: Swipe left to see the next photo.
She swiped her card at the store.
He's swiping through the pictures.

spanish.definition: Mover el dedo por una pantalla; pasar una tarjeta por una máquina.

definition: To become softer, or to make something softer.
examples: Butter softens at room temperature.
This cream softens your skin.
His face softened when he saw her.

spanish.definition: Volverse más suave, o hacer algo más suave.

definition: To judge how good something is.
examples: The teacher evaluated our work.
We need to evaluate the results.
They're evaluating all of the candidates.

spanish.definition: Juzgar qué tan bueno es algo.

definition: To go faster.
examples: The car accelerated on the highway.
She accelerated to pass the truck.
Global warming is accelerating.

spanish.definition: Ir más rápido.

definition: To write music, a poem, or a letter.
examples: Mozart composed this piece when he was young.
She composed a short email.
He's composing a song for his wife.

spanish.definition: Escribir música, un poema o una carta.

definition: To surprise someone very much.
examples: Her talent amazed everyone.
It amazes me how fast he learns.
The magician amazed the kids.

spanish.definition: Sorprender mucho a alguien.

definition: To make something harder to understand or do.
examples: Don't complicate things.
The rain complicated our plans.
You're complicating a simple problem.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más difícil de entender o de hacer.

definition: To give someone a disease.
examples: The virus infected thousands of people.
The cut got infected.
Sick workers are infecting others.

spanish.definition: Pasarle una enfermedad a alguien.

definition: To give official permission.
examples: Who authorized this payment?
The bank authorized the loan.
I'm authorizing you to sign for me.

spanish.definition: Dar permiso oficial.

definition: To become weaker, or to make something weaker.
examples: The illness weakened him.
The storm is weakening.
Too much sun can weaken your skin.

spanish.definition: Volverse más débil, o hacer algo más débil.

definition: To understand and care about someone's problems.
examples: I sympathize with you.
She sympathized with the workers.
We all sympathize with the families.

spanish.definition: Entender y preocuparse por los problemas de alguien.

definition: To make someone feel happy and full of energy.
examples: The news excited the kids.
Nothing excites me more than travel.
The idea of a trip excites her.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se sienta feliz y lleno de energía.

definition: To take something important away from someone.
examples: The prisoners were deprived of food.
He was deprived of sleep for days.
You're depriving her of a good education.

spanish.definition: Quitarle algo importante a alguien.

definition: To make something more active.
examples: Reading stimulates the mind.
The new tax stimulated the economy.
Coffee stimulates the brain.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más activo.

definition: To make a small, sudden movement.
examples: My eye keeps twitching.
The rabbit's nose twitched.
The dog twitches in its sleep.

spanish.definition: Hacer un movimiento pequeño y repentino.

definition: To move smoothly and quietly.
examples: The swan glided across the lake.
The skaters glided over the ice.
The bird is gliding on the wind.

spanish.definition: Moverse con suavidad y en silencio.

definition: To sit quietly and relax your mind.
examples: I meditate for ten minutes a day.
She meditated before the race.
He's meditating in the garden.

spanish.definition: Sentarse en silencio y relajar la mente.

definition: To start burning, or to make something start burning.
examples: The gas ignited with a loud bang.
A small spark ignited the fire.
Be careful, this liquid can ignite.

spanish.definition: Empezar a quemarse, o hacer que algo empiece a quemarse.

definition: To say the opposite of what someone said.
examples: Don't contradict your father.
His story contradicts the facts.
You're contradicting yourself.

spanish.definition: Decir lo contrario de lo que dijo alguien.

definition: To run very fast for a short distance; a short, fast race.
examples: She sprinted to catch the bus.
He won the 100-meter sprint.
We're sprinting to the finish line.

spanish.word: correr a toda velocidad / carrera corta
spanish.definition: Correr muy rápido una distancia corta; carrera corta y rápida.

definition: To take something away from someone officially.
examples: The teacher confiscated my phone.
Police confiscated the drugs.
They're confiscating all of the knives at the airport.

spanish.definition: Quitarle algo a alguien de forma oficial.

definition: To push a lot of things into a small space; to study a lot in a short time.
examples: He crammed his clothes into a bag.
She crammed for the test all night.
We're cramming five people into one car.

spanish.word: meter a la fuerza / estudiar a última hora
spanish.definition: Meter muchas cosas en un espacio pequeño; estudiar mucho en poco tiempo.

definition: To make something sharper.
examples: Can you sharpen this pencil?
He sharpened the knife.
She's sharpening her skills.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más afilado.

definition: To crash into something.
examples: Two cars collided on the bridge.
The bike collided with a truck.
The players collided during the game.

spanish.definition: Golpearse contra algo.

definition: To not include someone or something.
examples: The price excludes tax.
They excluded him from the group.
Stop excluding your sister from the game.

spanish.definition: No incluir a alguien o algo.

definition: To continue doing something; to continue to exist.
examples: If the pain persists, see your doctor.
She persisted until she got an answer.
The rain persisted all week.

spanish.definition: Seguir haciendo algo; seguir existiendo.

definition: To surprise and scare someone suddenly.
examples: You startled me!
The noise startled the horse.
Sorry, I didn't mean to startle you.

spanish.definition: Sorprender y asustar a alguien de repente.

definition: To become brighter or happier.
examples: Flowers can brighten a room.
His face brightened when he saw her.
Her call brightened my day.

spanish.definition: Volverse más luminoso o más alegre.

definition: To travel to work regularly; a trip to work.
examples: I commute by train.
She commutes two hours a day.
My commute is about thirty minutes.

spanish.definition: Viajar al trabajo regularmente; viaje al trabajo.

definition: To focus on one subject or type of work.
examples: The doctor specializes in children's health.
This store specializes in cheese.
She's specializing in criminal law.

spanish.definition: Enfocarse en un tema o tipo de trabajo.

definition: To stop being frozen.
examples: Thaw the chicken before you cook it.
The ice thawed in the spring.
The snow is thawing.

spanish.definition: Dejar de estar congelado.

definition: To stay in the air in one place.
examples: A helicopter hovered above the house.
The bird hovered over the flower.
Drones are hovering over the stadium.

spanish.definition: Quedarse en el aire en un mismo lugar.

definition: To bring people together again.
examples: The boy was reunited with his mother.
The band reunited after ten years.
They're reuniting the family for Christmas.

spanish.definition: Juntar otra vez a las personas.

definition: To officially suggest someone for a job or a prize.
examples: She was nominated for an Oscar.
The party nominated him for president.
We're nominating Maria as team leader.

spanish.definition: Proponer oficialmente a alguien para un trabajo o un premio.

definition: To make someone calm; to make pain less.
examples: She sang to soothe the baby.
This cream soothes dry skin.
Hot tea is soothing my throat.

spanish.definition: Tranquilizar a alguien; reducir el dolor.

definition: To be different; to change.
examples: Prices vary from store to store.
The weather varies a lot here.
The size of the classes varied last year.

spanish.definition: Ser diferente; cambiar.

definition: To push someone gently with your elbow.
examples: She nudged me to wake me up.
He gave me a little nudge.
The dog is nudging my hand.

spanish.definition: Empujar a alguien suavemente con el codo.

definition: To think that something is bad or wrong.
examples: Her parents disapprove of her boyfriend.
I disapprove of smoking in the house.
He disapproved of the plan.

spanish.definition: Pensar que algo es malo o incorrecto.

definition: To take small bites of something.
examples: The mouse nibbled the cheese.
She nibbled on a cookie.
He's nibbling his sandwich.

spanish.definition: Dar mordiscos pequeños a algo.

definition: To make someone less confident or less likely to do something.
examples: Don't let this discourage you.
His parents discouraged him from leaving school.
High prices are discouraging tourists.

spanish.definition: Quitarle confianza a alguien o hacer menos probable que haga algo.

definition: To annoy someone; to make part of the body sore.
examples: His voice irritates me.
Smoke irritates my eyes.
That soap is irritating my skin.

spanish.definition: Molestar a alguien; hacer que una parte del cuerpo arda o duela.

definition: To make something as small as possible.
examples: We need to minimize the risk.
Minimize the window on your screen.
She's minimizing the problem.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo lo más pequeño posible.

definition: To work together with someone.
examples: The two bands collaborated on a song.
We collaborate with other schools.
They're collaborating on a new book.

spanish.definition: Trabajar junto con alguien.

definition: To make someone want to do something.
examples: A good coach motivates his team.
What motivates you?
She's motivating the kids to read.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien quiera hacer algo.

definition: To destroy a building.
examples: They demolished the old factory.
The house will be demolished next week.
Workers are demolishing the bridge.

spanish.definition: Destruir un edificio.

definition: To make something shorter.
examples: Can you shorten these pants?
We shortened our trip by a day.
The days shorten in the fall.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más corto.

definition: To eat grass in a field.
examples: Cows were grazing in the field.
The sheep grazed on the hill.
Horses graze here in the summer.

spanish.definition: Comer hierba en un campo.

definition: To hear something by accident.
examples: I overheard them talking about me.
She overheard the conversation.
Sorry, I couldn't help overhearing.

spanish.definition: Escuchar algo por accidente.

definition: To show that something is important.
examples: The teacher emphasized the importance of reading.
He emphasized the last word.
She's emphasizing safety.

spanish.definition: Mostrar que algo es importante.

definition: To be very good at something.
examples: She excels at math.
He excelled in school.
Our team is excelling this year.

spanish.definition: Ser muy bueno para algo.
